bib.title: Chapter 6: Temporal-Difference Learning (Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, 2nd ed.)

question: How can value functions be learned from raw experience by bootstrapping (TD), for prediction and for on- and off-policy control?
contributions: TD(0) prediction and its advantages over MC and DP

limits: Tabular, one-step, model-free methods only (author's own wording in the summary).
No proof that TD learns faster than MC; stated as open question.
Random-walk and cliff curves are small gridworld/chain examples; alpha grids are in figures only.
Hyperparameters such as alpha in the cliff curves are not stated in the text.
practices: Use TD(0) instead of constant-alpha MC when episodes are long, continuing, or exploratory actions occur (Sec 6.2).
Use Expected Sarsa rather than Sarsa when the extra computation is affordable; it removes variance from choosing A_{t+1} (Sec 6.6).
Use two estimators (Double Q-learning) to avoid maximization bias (Sec 6.7).
Learn afterstate values when the immediate effect of actions is known (Sec 6.8).
